title: Cycles in graphs with at least as many edges as vertices
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex set $V$, and write $n$ for the number of vertices and $m$ for the number of edges of $G$. If $n \le m$, then $G$ contains a cycle: there exist a vertex $v$ and a closed walk from $v$ to $v$ that is a cycle.
hypotheses_covered: number of vertices is at most the number of edges
